title: Never microwave in plastic
body: Move food to glass or ceramic first. Microwave safe means the tub will not warp, not that nothing leaves it.

title: Filter, do not buy bottled
body: A PET bottle sheds into the water it holds, and more once it has been warm. A filter is cheaper by the second month.

title: Glass with glass lids
body: A glass tub with a plastic lid still puts plastic above hot food. The lid is the half people forget.

title: Wash cold
body: Thirty degrees instead of forty cut shedding by about thirty percent in testing. It is free and it is a setting.

title: Shoes off at the door
body: Soles are polyurethane and rubber, and every step abrades some of it onto your floor.

title: Skin is a better barrier than you think
body: Particles mostly do not cross intact skin. The concern is what dissolves into a lotion and absorbs.

title: Baby forces the exposure up
body: Smaller body, more contact, hand to mouth. Whatever the arithmetic says, treat baby items as high.

title: Say no bag first
body: Most cashiers hand you the items if you say it before they reach.

title: Keep a bag in the car
body: The one at home does not help at the shop.

title: BPA free is not plastic free
body: It says one monomer is absent. It says nothing about the rest.

title: Most cleaning needs soap and water
body: The rest is fragrance and marketing.

title: Let food cool before it goes in
body: Hot food into a plastic tub is the worst case in your kitchen. Ten minutes on the counter costs nothing.

title: Run the tap cold before drinking
body: Warm pipe water carries more of whatever the pipe is lined with. Ten seconds.

title: Decant the pantry
body: Rice, oats and flour come in plastic lined bags. Glass jars at home stop the long contact.

title: Full loads only
body: Less room means less friction between garments, and friction is what releases fibres.

title: Damp dust, never dry
body: Dry dusting lifts particles into the air you then breathe. A damp cloth traps them.

title: Fragrance is a legal umbrella
body: One word can stand for hundreds of ingredients. It is the concealment we count, not the scent.

title: Never warm a bottle in the microwave
body: Uneven heat and plastic in the same act.

title: Buy whole, not pre cut
body: A head of broccoli comes in its own packaging. A clamshell of florets does not.

title: Decline the receipt
body: Thermal paper is coated in BPS and it transfers to your fingers.

title: Plant based is a feedstock claim
body: Plant derived polyethylene is still polyethylene.

title: Skip the antibacterial spray at home
body: Quats are a formula question and you rarely need them.

title: Every 10°C roughly doubles it
body: That is the rate chemicals leach from plastic. It is why heat, not time, is the thing to design around.

title: Never leave bottled water in the car
body: Heat plus PET is the combination every study measures. If it has been baking, it is not the bottle to drink.

title: Beeswax wrap instead of cling film
body: For cheese, bread and half a lemon it does the same job and lasts a year.

title: Wash clothes less often
body: Jeans, sweaters and worn once shirts rarely need it. Fewer cycles is proportionally less shedding.

title: Ten minutes of open window
body: Indoor air is usually more concentrated than outdoor. Cross ventilate once a day.

title: Choose fragrance free, not unscented
body: Unscented often means a masking fragrance was added to cover the base smell.

title: Glass bottles with silicone sleeves
body: The sleeve solves the dropping problem the glass creates.

title: Skip produce bags for anything with skin
body: Apples, citrus, onions, potatoes, bananas, avocados.

title: Do not put receipts in your pocket
body: Or your mouth, or a child's hand.

title: Biodegradable needs conditions
body: Most need industrial heat that a home bin never reaches.

title: Bar dish soap has no bottle
body: And it lasts a surprisingly long time.

title: Takeaway comes out of the tub
body: Tip it onto a plate before it goes near the microwave. The container was built for transport, not heating.

title: Reverse osmosis for PFAS
body: Carbon alone does not reliably remove them. If PFAS is your worry, RO is the honest answer.

title: Stainless for the freezer
body: Freezer burn is about air, not the container. Steel and glass both work.

title: Air it instead
body: Most needs washing judgements are really needs airing. A few hours by an open window settles it.

title: Vacuum with a sealed system
body: If the machine is not sealed, the finest fraction goes through the motor and back into the room.

title: Leave on beats rinse off for risk
body: A lotion sits for hours. A wash is gone in a minute. Prioritise accordingly.

title: Polypropylene bottles at formula temperature
body: One study measured millions of particles per litre. Heat is the variable you control.

title: Bulk bins with a jar
body: Most stores will tare it at the till so you pay for contents only.

title: Take your own cup to the counter
body: Most places discount it and all of them allow it.

title: Compostable means industrially compostable
body: Unless it says home compostable, it will not.

title: Refill the spray bottle you own
body: The bottle is not the problem if you stop buying new ones.

title: Skip the plastic kettle
body: Boiling water in plastic is the highest temperature contact most kitchens have. Stainless or glass, and the water path matters more than the shell.

title: Check the certification, not the claim
body: NSF 53 and 401 mean tested. Filters chlorine taste means very little about anything else.

title: Leave headroom in glass
body: Liquids expand. Two centimetres stops a cracked jar.

title: Spot clean the one mark
body: A drop of dish soap on a damp cloth saves a whole cycle.

title: HEPA means the filter, not the machine
body: Check for a sealed True HEPA system, not the word HEPA on the box.

title: Check for microbeads
body: Polyethylene and polypropylene in a scrub. Banned in many places, still on some shelves.

title: Make the formula, then cool, then pour
body: If the bottle is plastic, do not mix hot in it.

title: The pause is the habit
body: Most household plastic comes home because nobody stopped to consider the alternative beside it.

title: Ask for the drink in a glass if you are staying
body: In is not the same as away.

title: Plastic neutral is a carbon offset
body: It is an accounting claim, not a material one.

title: Vinegar for limescale
body: Cheap, effective, and it comes in glass.

title: Check the lid, not just the jug
body: A glass kettle with a plastic lid interior still steams against plastic every boil.

title: Change the filter on time
body: An exhausted cartridge is worse than none, because it stops working while you keep trusting it.

title: Do not store bread in plastic
body: It sweats and goes mouldy faster. A linen bag or a box is better for the bread too.

title: Half the detergent
body: Fill lines are drawn to encourage overuse. Most loads need about half, and the bottle lasts twice as long.

title: Empty the vacuum outside
body: Emptying a bagless canister indoors undoes the vacuuming.

title: Bars remove the bottle
body: Shampoo, conditioner and soap bars skip the container question entirely.

title: Teethers go straight in the mouth
body: Natural rubber, wood or food grade silicone. Not soft PVC.

title: Before buying new, check what you own
body: The cupboard usually has a version of it already.

title: Carry a fork
body: A small steel one in a bag removes every plastic one you would be handed.

title: Natural is unregulated
body: It means whatever the marketing team decided.

title: Bicarbonate for scrubbing
body: No microbeads, no plastic pad.

title: No plastic spoon in a hot pan
body: Black plastic utensils are often recycled electronics, and they sit in the hottest part of the meal.

title: A stainless bottle with a plastic straw
body: Still plastic in the drink path. The straw is where your mouth is.

title: Zip bags are single use by design
body: The seal is the first thing to fail, and a failing seal is a shedding seal.

title: Air dry when you can
body: Tumble drying is heat plus tumbling, which is the shedding combination. A rack costs nothing to run.

title: Change filters on schedule
body: A loaded filter is a bypassed filter.

title: A safety razor lasts decades
body: One metal handle and cheap steel blades replaces a moulded cartridge every few weeks.

title: Squirty bath toys grow mould inside
body: They cannot be dried. That is the reason to skip them, before any plastic argument.

title: Before throwing out, ask if it has another use
body: A jar, a tin, a tub for the shed.

title: Refill before you leave the house
body: It removes the bottled water decision entirely.

title: Free from is a list of absences
body: It tells you nothing about what is present.

title: Cotton or linen cloths
body: Microfibre sheds plastic every wash.

title: Retire scratched nonstick
body: A worn coating sheds more than a new one. If it is scored, it has stopped being the pan you thought you bought.

title: Glass for anything acidic
body: Citrus water and cold brew sit against whatever holds them for hours.

title: Silicone bags for wet things
body: Reusable, dishwasher safe, and they do not crease into cracks the way plastic does.

title: A wash bag for synthetics
body: It catches fibres that would otherwise leave with the water. Use it for fleece above everything.

title: Doormats at both sides
body: One outside to knock off, one inside to catch. It halves what comes in.

title: Silk or PFAS free floss
body: Standard glide floss is often PTFE, and it is dragged between your gums.

title: Check the diaper topsheet
body: It is the layer against skin. No lotion, no fragrance, no aloe.

title: Before accepting free, ask if you will use it
body: Free samples and goody bags are how plastic arrives uninvited.

title: Say no to the straw when you order
body: After it is in the drink it is too late.

title: Check the ingredient list, not the front
body: The front is advertising. The back is required.

title: A wooden brush with natural bristles
body: It outlasts three plastic ones.

title: Wooden boards for hot food
body: A plastic board takes knife scars, and hot food into those grooves is contact you cannot wash out.

title: Do not refill a single use bottle
body: They were designed for one fill. Repeated washing and warmth is exactly what breaks them down.

title: Jars you already own
body: Passata and pickle jars are free food grade glass. Soak the label off and keep them.

title: Fleece is the worst offender
body: One jacket can shed thousands of fibres in a single wash. Wash it rarely and cold.

title: Carpet holds what hard floors release
body: It also releases it when disturbed. Vacuum slowly and often.

title: Bamboo handle, nylon bristles
body: The handle is honest and the bristles usually are not. Only animal hair is genuinely plastic free.

title: Chlorine free is not totally chlorine free
body: ECF still uses chlorine dioxide. TCF brands say TCF because it costs them more.

title: Loose tea over bags
body: Many bags are heat sealed with polypropylene, and they steep at boiling.

title: Airport security takes an empty bottle
body: Fill it on the other side.

title: A certification names a standard
body: If you cannot find the standard, it is a logo.

title: Coconut scour pads
body: No plastic mesh, and they compost.

title: Do not pour boiling water into a plastic jug
body: Filter pitchers included. Let it cool first, or filter cold.

title: Bottled water is not better tested
body: Municipal supply is tested more often and published. Bottled is a container question, not a purity one.

title: Label the lid, not the tub
body: Marker on plastic wears into the surface. Tape on the lid comes off clean.

title: Skip the dryer sheet
body: It is a fabric coated in fragrance and softener that transfers onto your clothes and into the air.

title: Children are on the floor
body: Floor dust is where the exposure concentrates for anyone crawling.

title: Toothpaste tubes are multilayer
body: Tablets and jars exist. The paste is the bigger question, but the tube is real.

title: Wipes are cloth plus liquid
body: The cloth is usually part plastic. It crosses the skin many times a day.

title: Buy the biggest size you will finish
body: One large container beats four small ones on packaging per use.

title: Picnic in steel and cloth
body: Everything reusable, nothing to bin.

title: OEKO-TEX covers textiles for substances
body: It is real, and it is narrow.

title: Do not use a magic eraser on food surfaces
body: It is melamine foam and it abrades.

title: Steam is contact too
body: A plastic lid above simmering food is in the food path even though it never touches the pan.

title: Watch the cooler bottle
body: Big office jugs are usually polycarbonate, which is the BPA one.

title: Cool before the fridge
body: Warm food in a sealed tub steams against the lid the entire time it cools.

title: Fabric softener coats fibres
body: It works by leaving a residue on the thing you wear all day.

title: Wash soft furnishings
body: Cushion covers and throws collect and release fibre.

title: Check sunscreen for the filter type
body: Mineral means zinc or titanium. Chemical filters are a different set of questions.

title: Plain water and a flannel at home
body: Wipes are for out of the house.

title: Concentrates ship less water
body: And you dilute into your own glass.

title: Hotel toiletries are single use
body: Bring a bar and leave them sealed.

title: GOTS covers organic fibre and processing
body: Also real, also specific.

title: Ventilate while you clean
body: Whatever is volatile concentrates in a closed room.

title: Cling film off before reheating
body: It sags onto the food as it warms. A plate on top does the same job.

title: Ice trays are contact too
body: Water freezes against the tray and picks up what it touches. Stainless or silicone.

title: Deli counter into your own tub
body: Most counters will fill a container you bring. Ask once and it becomes normal.

title: Wool needs almost no washing
body: It self freshens. Airing is the maintenance.

title: Fewer synthetic textiles in the bedroom
body: You spend eight hours with your face against your bedding.

title: Every mineral sunscreen has some lead
body: Zinc oxide is a mined mineral. A non zero number is the category baseline, not a scandal.

title: Cotton over synthetic for sleepwear
body: Eight hours of contact, every night.

title: Refill shops are worth one trip
body: Detergent, soap and oil in containers you already have.

title: Takeaway into your own container
body: Many places will fill one if you ask when ordering.

title: EWG Verified is a formula standard
body: It says nothing about the container.

title: Dilute concentrates into glass
body: Not into another plastic bottle.

title: Watch the rice cooker insert
body: Many have a coated bowl. Stainless inserts exist and outlast the machine.

title: Sparkling water in cans has a liner
body: Most cans are epoxy lined. Glass bottles skip the question.

title: Cheese needs to breathe
body: Waxed paper or a cheese bag. Plastic wrap makes it sweat.

title: Buy natural fibres when you replace
body: Cotton, linen, wool and hemp shed too, but they are not polymer.

title: Start with the pillowcase
body: It is the cheapest bedding swap and the closest to your face.

title: Deodorant is not antiperspirant
body: Aluminium salts are the antiperspirant part. If you only want to smell fine, you do not need them.

title: Flame resistant does not mean treated
body: Polyester passes by being polyester. Check whether chemicals were added.

title: Milk in glass where it exists
body: Returnable bottles are a closed loop.

title: Do not eat hot food from the lid
body: People do this with soup lids constantly.

title: MADE SAFE is broader and rarer
body: Worth knowing when you see it.

title: Dish soap does not need to be antibacterial
body: Hot water and agitation do the work.

title: Slow cookers run for hours
body: Long, warm contact is the same arithmetic as brief and hot. Check what the crock is lined with.

title: Fill from the tap, not the fridge door
body: Door dispensers run through plastic tubing that is rarely replaced.

title: Do not freeze in thin plastic
body: Cold makes plastic brittle, and brittle plastic flakes.

title: Check the label before you buy
body: Polyester, nylon, acrylic and elastane are plastic. The composition tag is the honest part of a garment.

title: Skip the plug in air freshener
body: It is a fragrance mixture aerosolised into a room you sleep in.

title: Watch the applicator
body: A plastic stick that touches skin daily is contact, even if the formula is clean.

title: Crib mattresses are mostly foam
body: Look for the certification that covers emissions, not just the fill.

title: Butcher and fishmonger take containers
body: Ask once. Most will.

title: Reheat leftovers at home, not in the box
body: The box came home for transport.

title: NSF numbers mean different things
body: 42 is taste, 53 is health contaminants, 401 is emerging ones.

title: Wash cloths hot and dry them flat
body: A damp cloth is the actual hygiene problem.

title: Air fryer baskets are coated
body: Hot air over a worn nonstick basket is the exposure this category is worst for.

title: Boil then cool in glass
body: If you boil for safety, do not cool it in plastic. That is where the heat meets the polymer.

title: Nested steel tins for lunch
body: No lid liner, no seal to fail, and they survive being dropped.

title: A filter on the machine
body: Retrofit lint filters catch a large share before the water leaves.

title: Candles are combustion
body: Even good ones. Ventilate after burning.

title: Nail polish is solvent chemistry
body: Ventilate, and treat it as an occasional thing rather than a weekly one.

title: Wash new baby clothes first
body: Finishes come off in the first wash.

title: Bread from a bakery in your own bag
body: Linen or paper, no plastic window.

title: Camping food in tins and jars
body: Foil pouches are multilayer plastic.

title: A disclosure is worth more than a claim
body: A brand publishing its layers is telling you more than one saying clean.

title: Skip the disposable wipe
body: It is a plastic cloth with a fragranced liquid on it.

title: Do not store fat in plastic
body: Oil is the strongest extractant in your kitchen. Oily leftovers belong in glass.

title: A pitcher lives in the fridge
body: Cold contact is the mildest kind. Keep the plastic pitcher cold if you keep it at all.

title: Dry goods do not need plastic
body: Paper, cloth and glass have stored grain for centuries. Plastic is a convenience, not a requirement.

title: Do not overload
body: Cramming increases friction and stops the machine rinsing properly.

title: Do not dry clothes indoors without ventilation
body: Damp air holds particles and grows mould.

title: Talc is on the hazard list
body: It appears in powders and some cosmetics. It is worth reading for by name.

title: Silicone bibs over plastic
body: Easier to clean and nothing flakes.

title: Farmers markets have less packaging by default
body: Not always cheaper, but usually barer.

title: Sun cream in the beach bag cooks
body: A hot bag is heat plus a leave on product.

title: No recall on record means nobody looked
body: Most of these categories are barely regulated.

title: Toilet cleaner does not need bleach every time
body: Bicarbonate and a brush most days.

title: Acidic food pulls more
body: Tomato sauce, citrus, vinegar. Same tub, more migration.

title: Test before you buy a filter
body: Your water report tells you what is actually in it. Buying for a contaminant you do not have is money spent for nothing.

title: Watch the freezer bag reused
body: Washing and refreezing is where a bag starts breaking down.

title: Shorter cycles shed less
body: Time in the drum is time abrading.

title: Check the extractor works
body: Kitchen and bathroom fans that vent outside remove more than any purifier.

title: Use up what you have
body: Throwing out a half used bottle to buy a cleaner one is waste, not progress.

title: Stainless plates and cups
body: They survive being thrown and they hold nothing.

title: Cans are lined, glass is not
body: For tomatoes and beans, the jar is the cleaner container.

title: Do not drink from a bottle left in the sun
body: Warm PET is the studied worst case.

title: A lawsuit is an allegation
body: A settlement is not an admission. Both are still worth knowing.

title: Check the laundry powder ingredients
body: Optical brighteners stay on the fabric by design.

title: Dishwasher heat ages plastic
body: The top rack is cooler for a reason. Repeated hot cycles are what turn a smooth tub cloudy.

title: Hydration powders come in sachets
body: The powder is the product; the sachet is usually multilayer plastic. Tubs are the lower packaging load.

title: Oil in dark glass
body: Light degrades the oil and the bottle is contact for months.

title: Line dry outdoors where you can
body: Sun and air, no heat, no tumbling.

title: Air purifiers help with fibre
body: But filter grade is the whole product. Coverage area is marketing.

title: Refills over new bottles
body: Same product, one container, many times.

title: Do not put a plastic plate in the dishwasher
body: Heat cycles are what age it.

title: Frozen is often less packaged than chilled
body: And it wastes less.

title: Sports drinks are the same bottle question
body: Plus sugar, but that is a different article.

title: Independent testing beats brand testing
body: Not because brands lie, but because they choose the questions.

title: Fragrance free cleaning is easier on everyone
body: Especially in a small flat.

title: A cloudy tub has changed
body: Crazing is the surface breaking down. That is the point to retire it, whatever the date on it.

title: Do not store water in the garage
body: Warm, long storage is the worst combination for any plastic container.

title: Herbs and spices in glass
body: Small tins and jars. Spice bags are usually lined.

title: New clothes shed most
body: The first few washes release the highest number of fibres. Wash new synthetics separately if you filter.

title: Houseplants do not clean the air
body: The studies were sealed chambers. Ventilation does the work.

title: Cotton buds with paper stems
body: A small thing, but it is a plastic stick you use once.

title: Bamboo melamine is melamine
body: The bamboo is filler; the binder is the exposure, and it migrates at heat.

title: Do not buy for a future you are guessing at
body: Most impulse kitchenware ends up unused and plastic.

title: Wet swimwear in a bag all day
body: Warm, damp, synthetic. Rinse and air it instead.

title: Non detect depends on the detection limit
body: Ask what the limit was before trusting the result.

title: A squeegee beats a spray
body: For shower glass, water and a blade is enough.

title: Wash plastic by hand, cool
body: If you keep a tub, cool water and a soft cloth extend its honest life.

title: Kettle water sits between boils
body: Reboiling in a plastic kettle repeats the contact. Empty it if it will sit.

title: Buy bulk with your own jars
body: Most stores will tare a jar at the till. You pay for contents only.

title: Second hand skips the shedding peak
body: Someone else already put it through its first washes.

title: Dust the tops of things
body: Wardrobes and door frames hold years of it and release it in a draught.

title: Wet wipes are usually plastic cloth
body: Polyester or polypropylene, and the cloth is the exposure, not the liquid.

title: Pouches are multilayer plastic
body: With acidic puree inside, often warmed. Jars skip all of it.

title: Check the returns policy before you buy online
body: A returned item usually gets repackaged.

title: Gym bottles get chewed and warm
body: Steel survives both.

title: One test is a snapshot
body: Formulations change and suppliers change.

title: Do not mix cleaners
body: Genuinely dangerous, and unrelated to plastic.

title: Kettle descaling is not cleaning
body: Scale is minerals. The plastic is a separate question and descaling does not touch it.

title: Filter for the whole house, or the tap you drink from
body: Whole house helps the shower; a tap filter helps what you swallow. They are different problems.

title: A big jar beats many small tubs
body: Fewer lids, fewer seals, less to fail.

title: Mend before replacing
body: The lowest impact garment is the one you already own.

title: Wash curtains twice a year
body: They filter your window air and hold what they catch.

title: A flannel and water
body: For most face washing this is genuinely enough.

title: Make it and freeze it in trays
body: Silicone trays, then transfer to glass.

title: Choose the pick with the fewest layers
body: Box inside film inside tray is three decisions somebody made.

title: Office coffee is usually a pod machine
body: A press at your desk takes two minutes.

title: Fragrance and parfum are the same word
body: And both mean undisclosed.

title: Rags from old cotton
body: The best cleaning cloth is a worn out t shirt.

title: Reheat in the oven where you can
body: No plastic, no scratched coating, and better food. Slower is the only cost.

title: Shower filters are about chloramine
body: Not microplastics. Buy one for the right reason.

title: Do not microwave the lid
body: Even if the tub is fine, the lid is usually a softer plastic.

title: Detergent sheets and bars exist
body: No jug, no measuring cap, no plastic bottle in the cupboard.

title: Mattresses shed too
body: A washable protector in cotton is easier than replacing the mattress.

title: Loofah means the gourd
body: If it is foam, it is plastic, whatever the label calls it.

title: Check car seat flame retardants
body: Testing has found brominated and chlorinated treatments across major brands.

title: Delivery adds packaging
body: Collecting in person removes a layer you never see.

title: Bring lunch in glass
body: It reheats without transferring.

title: Essential oils named individually is disclosure
body: Linalool and limonene declared is more honest than fragrance.

title: Wooden pegs and cotton line
body: Plastic pegs go brittle in the sun and snap into fragments.

title: Silicone is not plastic, but check the grade
body: Food grade silicone is stable at heat. Cheap fillers are what make a cheap mould smell.

title: Watch cold brew in plastic
body: Twelve hours of contact, and coffee is acidic. Glass jar, every time.

title: Vacuum sealing is still plastic
body: Great for freezer burn, no help at all for contact.

title: Do not dry clean unless you must
body: Perc is a solvent, and the film bag it comes home in is plastic on clean clothes.

title: Do not shake bedding indoors
body: You are aerosolising a week of dust into the room.

title: Check period products for the cover
body: Topsheets can be plastic even when the core is cotton.

title: Air a new car seat outdoors
body: Off gassing is highest when new and in heat.

title: Buy once
body: The cheapest version bought three times costs more and sheds more.

title: Travel with a cloth bag for laundry
body: Hotel plastic bags are a habit, not a need.

title: Hypoallergenic has no legal definition
body: It is a marketing word.

title: Compost the brush head
body: If it is wood and bristle, it goes in the bin that matters.

title: Parchment beats a plastic liner
body: For baking, unbleached parchment does the job without a coating.

title: Refill stations beat cases
body: One good bottle and a refill habit removes an entire category of purchase.

title: Check what a compostable liner is
body: Many are PLA, which needs an industrial composter and behaves like plastic at home.

title: Take the film off immediately
body: If it does come back in a bag, hang it out of it.

title: Vent the tumble dryer outside
body: Dryer exhaust is fibre. Condensing dryers keep it in the house.

title: Cups and discs are silicone
body: Medical grade silicone is stable and lasts years.

title: Wooden toys need no coating question
body: Untreated hardwood is the simplest answer in the toy box.

title: Second hand for anything hard
body: Cast iron, glass, steel and wood do not wear out.

title: Beach: leave with more than you brought
body: Not exposure, but it is the same instinct.

title: Dermatologist tested says nothing about the result
body: Tested, not passed.

title: Buy cleaning tools once
body: A good brush is a decade purchase.

title: Do not leave utensils in the pot
body: A plastic handle resting against a hot rim is the same contact, just quieter.

title: Frozen bottles crack invisibly
body: Freezing stresses PET. The bottle you refroze is not the bottle you bought.

title: Cast iron and steel do not need liners
body: A well seasoned pan stores nothing and releases nothing.

title: Iron on lower heat for synthetics
body: Heat on polyester is the same principle as heat on a food tub.

title: Beat rugs outdoors
body: Not in the hallway.

title: Shower curtains: fabric over vinyl
body: A PEVA or PVC liner off gasses in a warm wet room.

title: Second hand toys are pre off gassed
body: And usually cheaper.

title: Read the material, not the marketing
body: Bamboo, plant based and eco are not material claims.

title: Rental cars off gas in heat
body: Open the windows before the air conditioning.

title: Food grade is a use claim
body: It means approved for contact, not that nothing migrates.

title: Empty the vacuum before it is full
body: A full bag pushes air past the filter.

title: Glass jars take hot fills
body: Wide mouth jars handle hot soup fine if you warm them first. Cold glass plus boiling liquid cracks.

title: Water in a hydration bladder
body: Long storage, warm, flexible plastic. Empty and dry it between uses.

title: Glass in the oven, with care
body: Borosilicate handles heat. Tempered soda lime does not like sudden change.

title: Wash bedding in cotton loads
body: Mixing a fleece throw with your sheets moves fibres onto what you sleep on.

title: Microfibre cloths shed
body: Ironic but true. Cotton or linen for cleaning cloths.

title: Ventilate the bathroom
body: Warm, humid and enclosed is where anything volatile concentrates.

title: Do not microwave a sippy cup
body: Same rule as everything else, and they get microwaved a lot.

title: A shopping list halves impulse buys
body: Less bought is less packaging, with no other effort.

title: Microwave safe means it will not warp
body: That is genuinely all it means.

title: Coffee pods are hot plastic
body: A single pod meets water near boiling. A press, pour over or moka pot skips it entirely.

title: Check the lid liner
body: Metal bottle caps are usually lined. It is a small area, but it is in the drink path.

title: Do not stack hot jars
body: Trapped heat is prolonged heat, and the seal is where it concentrates.

title: A drying rack in a warm room
body: Ventilate it and it dries as fast as a machine in most weather.

title: Check the car cabin filter
body: Cars are small sealed rooms full of synthetic textiles.

title: Hair tools get very hot
body: Plastic barrels and combs against heat is the same rule as the kitchen.

title: Replace chewed spouts
body: A chewed valve is a shedding valve.

title: Take the packaging off at the shop where you can
body: Some stores have a bin for it and it makes the point.

title: Recyclable depends on your council
body: The triangle is a resin code, not a promise.

title: Skip the lined to-go cup
body: The waterproof layer is polyethylene, and hot coffee sits against it the whole walk.

title: Do not drink from a hose
body: Garden hoses are not made to food standards and sit in the sun all day.

title: Baby food into glass
body: Pouches are multilayer plastic against acidic puree, and that combination is the one Consumer Reports measured phthalates in.

title: Sort by fabric, not just colour
body: Rough and synthetic together, soft and natural together. Less abrasion both ways.

title: Open the window in the car first
body: Let the interior off gas before you set off, especially in heat.

title: Do not store cosmetics in the sun
body: A windowsill shelf cooks whatever is in the bottle.

title: Nursing pillows are foam
body: A cotton cover you can wash is the practical middle.

title: Loose eggs in your own box
body: Reuse the same carton for years.

title: Number 7 is other
body: It is the catch all, and it includes polycarbonate.

title: Bring the cup you already own
body: No purchase needed. The cup in your cupboard is the upgrade.

title: Fluoride is a separate question
body: Most filters do not remove it. If that matters to you, check specifically.

title: Silicone freezer trays for portions
body: Pop out, transfer to glass, done.

title: Front loaders are gentler
body: Less agitation than a top loader with a central post.

title: Radiators bake the dust behind them
body: Clean behind them before the heating goes on.

title: Check lip products first
body: Anything on lips is partly swallowed. Start your reading there.

title: Change mats are usually PVC
body: A cotton towel over one solves most of it.

title: Avoid single serve anything
body: Portion packs multiply packaging by the number of servings.

title: A long ingredient list is not automatically worse
body: A short one you cannot check is worse.

title: Kettles with exposed elements
body: A bare stainless element in contact with the water is preferable to a plastic housed one.

title: A carafe on the table
body: Decant into glass at mealtimes. It is the easiest swap in the house.

title: Wooden bowls for dry food
body: Nothing migrates from dry contact at room temperature.

title: Check pockets for receipts
body: Thermal paper in the wash spreads BPS through the load.

title: A robot vacuum daily beats a deep clean weekly
body: Frequency matters more than power for settled dust.

title: Simpler lists are easier to check
body: Six ingredients you can read beats thirty you cannot.

title: Baby lotion is leave on
body: It is the highest contact personal care product in the house.

title: Sauces and condiments in glass
body: They sit in the fridge for months, which is long contact.

title: If a claim cannot be checked, treat it as marketing
body: That is the whole method in one line.

title: Kids bottles get chewed
body: A chewed spout is a shedding spout. Replace the part, not the bottle.

title: Metal tins for biscuits
body: The tin your grandmother kept is still the right answer.

title: Do not tumble dry towels to death
body: Every cycle takes fibre off them. That is what the lint is.

title: Do not use a leaf blower on the patio
body: You are moving the dust to head height.

title: Patch test anything new
body: Not a plastic point, just sense.

title: Fragrance free everything for babies
body: There is no upside to a scent on a newborn.

title: Do not stockpile in the garage
body: Warm long storage is the worst case for packaging.

title: Sports bottle valves are soft plastic
body: Soft means it degrades faster. Check them every few months.

title: Do not store citrus in plastic
body: Acid plus oil in the peel is the most extracting combination in the fruit bowl.

title: Rinse twice if you use less detergent
body: It is a better trade than more detergent and one rinse.

title: Wet mop hard floors
body: Sweeping redistributes; mopping removes.

title: Body oil after a shower
body: One ingredient, no emulsifier, no preservative system needed.

title: Sunscreen from six months
body: Before that, shade and clothing.

title: Check unit price, not pack price
body: It usually points at the less packaged option too.

title: Warm juice cartons are lined
body: The carton is paper over polyethylene. Cold storage is doing more work than you think.

title: Keep the pantry cool
body: Every degree in a warm cupboard speeds up whatever is happening in the packaging.

title: Store clean laundry out of plastic
body: Vacuum bags and under bed boxes hold clothes against plastic for months.

title: Change bedding weekly
body: It is the highest contact textile in the house.

title: Solid perfume in a tin
body: Skips the alcohol, the sprayer and the plastic.

title: Check bath toys for a hole
body: If water gets in, it stays in.

title: Bring a bag you will actually carry
body: One that folds into a pocket beats a tote left at home.

title: Boiling does not remove plastic
body: It removes microbes. Filtration is the mechanism for particles.

title: Rinse and reuse the good jars
body: A jar that held tomato sauce holds soup just as well.

title: Moth protection without the block
body: Cedar and lavender, not paradichlorobenzene.

title: Ventilate while you cook
body: Cooking is the biggest particle event of most days.

title: Glass droppers over plastic pipettes
body: The dropper sits in the product for months.

title: Bottle brushes shed too
body: A brush with natural bristles cleans just as well.

title: Ask brands directly
body: A brand that will not tell you what is in the topsheet has told you something.

title: One bottle, not six
body: A cupboard of half used bottles is how plastic accumulates. Own one you actually like.

title: Buy the concentrate
body: Less water shipped is less packaging per use, and you dilute into glass at home.

title: The laundry room is likely your biggest source
body: One load can release six figures of fibres. This is the room where free changes do most.

title: Keep the bedroom door open in the day
body: Still air concentrates whatever is in the room.

title: Do not decant into travel plastic
body: Small plastic bottles in a warm washbag is a lot of contact for a week away.

title: Sterilising is heat plus plastic
body: If you sterilise, do it in a way that does not cook the bottle.

title: One good pan beats a set
body: Sets are how coated cookware enters a kitchen.

title: Check the container before the food
body: For pantry staples the container is usually the bigger question.

title: Bar soap in a dish, not a bag
body: It lasts longer dry and there is nothing to throw away.

title: Paper bags for mushrooms
body: They need to breathe and plastic makes them slimy.

title: Check the preservative, not just the actives
body: Formaldehyde releasers hide behind names like DMDM hydantoin.

title: A bread bin is not nostalgia
body: It keeps bread better than any bag, and there is nothing to throw away.

title: Sunscreen expiry is real
body: The filters degrade. An old bottle protects less.

title: Do not decant into plastic
body: If you are moving food out of a bag, move it into glass, not another tub.

title: Reef safe is not a safety claim
body: It is about coral, and it is unregulated.

title: Airtight matters more than material for dry goods
body: But when the two conflict, glass wins.

title: Read the last three ingredients
body: Fragrance and preservatives sit at the end, and that is where the questions are.
